one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent lacked knowledge that fastText model size is dominated by the bucket/hash parameter (default 2M entries), so all models trained with reduced dim/epochs remained hundreds of MB over the 150MB limit, and subsequent quantization attempts caused an unrecoverable terminal hang.
t_err_evidence: At step 37, after discovering the first model is 1.4GB, the agent decided to retrain with only dim=50 (down from 100) and epoch=5 (down from 10), not realizing that the default bucket parameter (2,000,000 hash bins) is the dominant factor in fastText model size; the correct fix was to drastically reduce -bucket or -minCount, not just dimensions.
t_commit_evidence: At step 83, the agent queued a fresh training command (dim=20, epoch=5) inside a frozen terminal that already had multiple unexecuted quantization commands buffered; from this point the terminal was permanently stuck showing only 'fasttext supervised...' in the buffer with no way to recover.
t_surface_evidence: At step 74, the agent explicitly notes that the quantization command 'appears to be hanging or taking longer than expected' and starts queuing alternative commands without being able to interrupt the frozen terminal.
trigger_explanation: The agent did not know that fastText supervised model size is primarily controlled by the bucket parameter (default 2,000,000), not embedding dimension. With 1.6M vocab words and 2M buckets at even dim=20, the model output matrix alone exceeds 150MB. Correct approach required using -bucket 100000 or aggressive quantization; instead the agent only tuned dim and epoch, producing models that remained 448-1400MB.
forewarning_evidence: Step 37: model.bin was 1.4GB (first warning that size reduction strategy was insufficient). Steps 55-60: model_small at 724MB still oversized. Step 70: model_tiny at 448MB still oversized. All three results indicated the approach of reducing dim/epoch alone could not reach 150MB.
